document_check.note: Document is Wearn AR, Nurdal V, Saunders-Jennings E, et al. 'T2 heterogeneity as an in vivo marker of microstructural integrity in medial temporal lobe subfields in ageing and mild cognitive impairment', NeuroImage 238 (2021) 118214. Authors, year and the cited finding (T2 heterogeneity and entorhinal volume predicting one-year cognitive decline in MCI, overall models not significant) all match the citing sentence.

cited_result: Section 3.3: in the MCI subgroup followed up at one year, forward stepwise regressions (adjusted for age and baseline cognition) found CA1-3 T2 heterogeneity (beta -0.605, p = .025; EC T2 heterogeneity similar, beta -0.567, p = .031) and EC volume (beta 0.595, p = .030) to be individual predictors of follow-up cognition, while absolute T2 entered no predictor; neither overall model was significant (p = .074 and p = .087).
tool_reason: The cited result is the association of a baseline imaging factor (T2 heterogeneity, subfield volume) with a later outcome (one-year cognitive change) in regression models adjusted for covariates; it is not the discrimination or calibration of a prediction model, so QUIPS fits.

domains.rationale: Source population and recruitment routes are described and MCI is defined by Petersen criteria, but recruitment is a convenience mix (clinics, research register, posters, word of mouth), participation rates are not reported, and 7 of the MCI group were reclassified from controls on a MoCA cut-off alone, so the MCI sample is heterogeneous.

signalling.question: Is the source population and method of recruitment adequately described?
signalling.quote: Subjects for both studies were recruited from local GP surgeries and memory clinics in the Bristol area (having received MCI diagnoses or reported memory problems), Join Dementia Research, Avon and Wilt- shire Mental Health Partnership’s Everyone Included system, an in- house database of volunteers, replies to poster adverts or through word of mouth.

signalling.question: Are inclusion criteria for the MCI group adequately defined and applied consistently?
signalling.quote: 7 participants origi- nally recruited as healthy controls in study 1 were found to have MoCA scores of < 26, so were reclassiﬁed as MCI

signalling.question: Is the MCI diagnostic standard stated?
signalling.quote: Participants fulﬁlling the Petersen criteria ( Albert et al., 2011 ) for diagnosis of MCI were recruited to both studies (Study 1: n = 30, Study 2: n = 29).

signalling.question: Was there adequate participation by eligible persons (participation rate reported)?
signalling.quote: Searched Methods and Results for the number of people approached, eligible or declining; none reported.

domains.rationale: Only 20 of 49 MCI participants (41%) contributed follow-up data; reasons were not recorded and the authors state that dropout was sometimes due to decline, so the lost participants likely differ from completers on the outcome; no comparison of completers and non-completers is reported.

signalling.question: Is the proportion of the baseline sample available for analysis adequate?
signalling.quote: A total of 20 MCI participants were followed-up after one-year (10 from each study), rep- resenting a relatively high dropout rate from the MCI cohort.

signalling.question: Are reasons for loss to follow-up provided?
signalling.quote: Although reasons for not returning were never formally quantiﬁed, this was occasionally due to the participant feeling unable to attend the sec- ond session due to signiﬁcant cognitive and/or functional decline.

signalling.question: Were participants lost to follow-up similar to completers in key characteristics?
signalling.quote: Those who declined the most may therefore be simply missed out of the cur- rent analyses.

domains.rationale: T2 heterogeneity is clearly defined and measured automatically at baseline (before the outcome), but the segmentation method is not validated for T2 heterogeneity, and the two cohorts used different quantitative T2 sequences that give different values, combined only by within-cohort z-scoring of about 10 participants each.

signalling.question: Is a clear definition of the prognostic factor provided?
signalling.quote: T2 distribution histograms were modelled as loglogistic distributions within each subﬁeld

signalling.question: Is the method of measurement adequately valid and reliable?
signalling.quote: We acknowledge that our masking procedure of hippocampal sub- ﬁelds (automated using ASHS) has only been veriﬁed for measuring shape and volume, not T2 heterogeneity.

signalling.question: Was the same method of measurement used for all participants?
signalling.quote: The two distinct methods of measuring quantitative T2 (CPMG vs TSE) will give inherently diﬀerent values for T2 midpoint and hetero- geneity between studies

signalling.question: Are continuous factors handled appropriately (no arbitrary cut-points)?
signalling.quote: Z-scores for this analysis were calculated relative to each study’s MCI population only.

signalling.question: Was the factor measured without knowledge of the outcome?
signalling.quote: ASHS has demonstrated high accuracy whilst minimising subjective rater bias, without the need for group blinding

domains.rationale: The outcome (follow-up cognition adjusted for baseline) is clearly defined and uses standard screening instruments, but the two cohorts used different instruments (MoCA vs ACE-III) pooled by z-scoring, and blinding of cognitive testers to imaging is not reported.

signalling.question: Is a clear definition of the outcome provided?
signalling.quote: We entered follow-up cognition as the dependant variable and baseline cognition and age as ﬁxed covariates

signalling.question: Was the same outcome measurement method used for all participants?
signalling.quote: Cognitive function was tested at baseline and follow-up using the MoCA in study 1 and the ACE-III in study 2.

signalling.question: Was the outcome assessed without knowledge of the prognostic factor?
signalling.quote: Searched Methods for blinding of cognitive assessors to MRI findings; not reported.

domains.rationale: Age and baseline cognition are adjusted for, which addresses the main confounders of follow-up cognition, but education (which differed between groups), cohort/sequence and amyloid or other biomarker status are not accounted for; the authors note co-pathologies are likely.

signalling.question: Were important potential confounders measured?
signalling.quote: The main limitation is the lack of biomarker status availability for people with MCI in this study

signalling.question: Were important confounders accounted for in the analysis?
signalling.quote: whilst always accounting for baseline cognitive score and age

domains.rationale: With about 20 participants, forward stepwise selection among six regions per modality across three modalities, entry at p < .05 and no multiplicity correction, the individual predictor p-values are highly prone to chance and optimism; the overall models were not significant, and the reported degrees of freedom are inconsistent with the stated 20 participants followed up. All three modality models are reported, which limits selective reporting.

signalling.question: Is the strategy for model building appropriate?
signalling.quote: The criteria for adding more variables was a signiﬁ- cant F statistic at the p < .05 level.

signalling.question: Is there sufficient presentation of data to assess the analysis?
signalling.quote: Age and baseline cog- nition alone were unable to signiﬁcantly predict follow-up cognitive score ( R 2 = 0.092, F (2, 19) = 0.859, p = .441; AIC = 29.9).

signalling.question: Is the interpretation supported by the overall model?
signalling.quote: However, the overall model was not sta- tistically signiﬁcant ( R 2 = 0.344, F (3, 19) = 2.79, p = .074, AIC = 25.4), indi- cating relatively weak predictive power.

signalling.question: Was multiplicity addressed?
signalling.quote: Where possible we have used comprehensive models, to minimise the need for multiple compari- son corrections.

signalling.question: Is there no selective reporting of results?
signalling.quote: Absolute T2 was unable to predict cognitive decline over the year, with no subﬁelds being entered into this model.

overall_rationale: By the brief's QUIPS rule the overall rating is high because two domains are high: attrition (59% of the MCI cohort lost, likely differentially by decline) and statistical analysis (stepwise selection in about 20 participants, non-significant overall models, no multiplicity control); participation, factor measurement, outcome measurement and confounding each carry moderate concerns.
